topics.topic: Numeric bound and setrlimit resource for the per-file scratch-size limit
questions: Which numeric bound must the runner use for the maximum size of one file written in the scratch?
Which bound supplies the setrlimit value for the size of a file written in scratch, since ResourceBounds M04 contains no scratch-file-size field?
Which bound and which `setrlimit` resource govern the size of one scratch file, given that M04 has no scratch-file-size field?

judgement.why: This asks the same per-file scratch setrlimit bound question as P1, and its deciding later-state passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Numeric bound for the per-file scratch setrlimit
quotes: execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] The runner MUST set every setrlimit limit inside the sandbox's user namespace before it loads the code, soft and hard alike (every limit is set soft and hard to the same value; bubblewrap is started without any capability option, so the code holds none and cannot raise a limit): address space at bounds.memory_bytes, the size of a file written in the scratch at the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant, and the outer process bound, the limit on the number of processes at bounds.process_count + 1;
precedent.why: The State 8 notes specify that the per-file scratch setrlimit uses RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX.

topics.topic: Ownership and documentation of parent-side aggregate scratch-total enforcement
questions: Is enforcement of the aggregate scratch total an outside-parent responsibility owned by `module:sandbox`, and must it be included in the module responsibility text?
Is the scratch-total limit enforced by the parent outside the environment, or by the runner inside it?
Does `module:sandbox` also own and implement the parent's scratch-total enforcement, which the changed State 3 ownership summary omits?

judgement.why: This asks the same module ownership and parent-side aggregate scratch enforcement question as P2, and its deciding later-state passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Module ownership of external scratch-total-limit enforcement
quotes:
`module:sandbox`. Execute one implementation on one input set in a fresh isolated environment and
name how it ended.

one fresh private exchange directory bound read-write whose use is bounded by the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant twice — each file written in it by the runner's setrlimit file-size limit, and the bytes the code adds to the whole directory by the parent, which measures them while it waits and kills the environment as a resource hit once they exceed that constant —, bubblewrap's own fresh proc and minimal dev mounts, and no other host directory;
precedent.why: The later API and implementation notes place execute_function in module:sandbox and require its parent process to enforce the total scratch limit.

topics.topic: Outcome when parent-side scratch-total enforcement cannot be established or maintained
questions: What happens if the parent cannot establish or maintain scratch-total enforcement, since the stated `crashed` outcome covers only a runner that cannot set its limits?
